_help.what: Curated details that GitHub cannot store. Everything here is optional — a repo with no entry still renders from its API data alone.

keys.featured: Repo names pinned to the home page, in this order.
keys.hidden: Repo names never shown anywhere on the site.
keys.overrides: Per-repo curation, keyed by the exact repository name.

overrideFields.tagline: One line shown on the card. Falls back to the GitHub description.
overrideFields.longDescription: Shown on the detail page. Supports **bold**, *italic*, `code`, [links](https://example.com), - bullet lists and # headings.
overrideFields.status: One of: live, beta, wip, paused, archived, experiment. Otherwise inferred.
overrideFields.demoUrl: Live demo URL. Use the literal 'self' to point at this site (it follows wherever you deploy). Falls back to the repo's GitHub homepage field.
overrideFields.embeddable: true to render the demo in an iframe on the page. Leave false if the site sends X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors, or it will show a blank box.
overrideFields.media: Screenshots/GIFs shown when the demo cannot be embedded. Paths are relative to public/, e.g. 'media/app-1.png'.
overrideFields.techStack: Overrides the stack derived from languages and topics.
overrideFields.lookingForHelp: Flags the project as open to contributors.
overrideFields.helpNotes: One or two sentences on what specifically needs doing.
overrideFields.hideReadme: true to omit the README section on the detail page.

_help.alsoNote: A repository can set its own status with a GitHub topic like 'status-live' or 'status-wip', which is handy for repos you do not want to list here.

Bouncing-Ball.tagline: A coordinate-geometry bouncing ball simulation you can run in the browser.
Bouncing-Ball.longDescription:
A ball bouncing under simple physics, worked out from coordinate geometry rather than a game engine.

The repository holds a Python (turtle) version; the demo above is the browser build, drawn on a `<canvas>` with the physics in a separate module.

TheColloborator.tagline: This site — a self-updating showcase of my GitHub projects.
TheColloborator.longDescription:
The site you are looking at right now.

A GitHub profile is a list of repository names. It does not tell you which projects are finished, which you can actually try, or which would welcome help. The Collaborator is the page that answers those questions.

The project list is read straight from the GitHub API, so pushing a new repository is enough to make it appear here — there is no list to maintain by hand. A small curated file adds what GitHub cannot store: status, demo URL, screenshots, and what specifically needs doing.

It is a static Angular app with no backend. Feature ideas become GitHub issues, and the offline snapshot means the page still renders when the API is rate-limited.
TheColloborator.helpNotes: Ideas for what a project showcase should surface are especially welcome — as are screenshots and better descriptions for any project listed here.
